title: Postural Activation
opening: For a task you choose, try working while seated or standing. Notice your comfort and how the setup works for that task.

labels.stationPrompt: Use the same comfort-and-task question in a seated or standing arrangement.
labels.sceneFigure: Illustrative articulated person in the selected work position; no posture score or outcome is shown.
labels.signalPrompt: Choose one factor to inspect in your task.
labels.practice: Apply this to your own task

stations.label: Seated work
stations.sceneLabel: Person seated on a chair at a desk, writing in a notebook.

stations.label: Standing work
stations.sceneLabel: Person standing in a work position.

signals.label: My position feels unsupported
signals.first: If a different position feels comfortable, try a light adjustment. Let the shoulders settle without holding a rigid pose.
signals.observe: Notice comfort and tension separately. Then notice whether the task itself is easier to take part in.
signals.change: If the adjustment increases discomfort or brings no useful change, change the arrangement or stop using that cue.

signals.label: Screen or surface feels awkward
signals.first: Inspect the equipment or work surface. Adjusting it may address the difficulty more directly than repeatedly reminding yourself to change posture.
signals.observe: Notice whether the new placement is comfortable and supports the task. Alertness is a separate observation.
signals.change: If the placement does not help the task or makes comfort worse, change it again or choose another factor to inspect.

signals.label: Tension grows as the task continues
signals.first: Inspect how long you have been working and whether the task arrangement needs to change. A posture cue is not a universal explanation for tension.
signals.observe: Notice comfort, tension, and task participation separately. The source gives no required interval or dose.
signals.change: If discomfort increases or the task is not supported, stop or change the arrangement; do not treat pain as progress.

practice.prediction: For one task you choose, what would you want the arrangement to support?
practice.observation: What is your current position, and what discomfort or tension do you notice, if any?
practice.comparison: Which factor will you inspect first: posture, equipment placement, or task duration? What makes it relevant to your task?
practice.result: After any comfortable adjustment, what did you notice about comfort, tension, and the task? Keep these observations separate.
practice.revision: If discomfort increased or nothing useful changed, what different arrangement or factor would you try?
practice.step: How will you tell whether the arrangement feels comfortable and supports your participation in the task?

feedback.unavailable: Private notes are unavailable here. Your answers remain in this session.
feedback.missing: Write about your task, the factor you will inspect, and how you will judge comfort and task participation before saving.
feedback.length: Shorten each answer to 2,000 characters or fewer.
feedback.readFailure: Your saved notes could not be loaded. Your current answers remain here.
feedback.conflict: These notes changed elsewhere. Your answers remain here. Save again to keep them.

feedback.saveFailure: The save is uncertain. Retry the same answers.
